visual_text: In this inquiry, median age at death was 13 years lower for men and 20 years lower for women
Learning disability, south-west England, 247 deaths in 2010 to 2012
About 37 in 100 of these deaths were from causes good health care can usually treat, against 13 in 100 in the general population.
Going into hospital: three things to ask for
The learning disability liaison nurse or team
The hospital passport: a record of the person's needs
The person who knows them best, listened to
About 1 in 3 adults with a learning disability whose deaths in English hospitals (2016 to 2021) were reviewed had input from a learning disability liaison nurse.
Sheehan et al., BMJ Open 2024; Heslop et al., Lancet 2014
alt_text: Card 1: median age at death in a south-west England learning disability inquiry of 247 deaths in 2010 to 2012. Men 65 versus 78 in the general population, 13 years lower; women 63 versus 83, 20 years lower. About 37 in 100 deaths were from treatable causes versus 13 in 100.

Card 2: three things to ask for on going into hospital: the learning disability liaison nurse or team, the hospital passport, and the person who knows them best, listened to. About 1 in 3 reviewed hospital deaths had liaison nurse input.
